meta.title: hoi an & danang: how to spend 5 days in central vietnam
meta.description:
#hoian #danang #vietnamtravel #travelvlog #hoianancienttown #vietnamvlog #centralvietnam  

we fell in love with hoi an and danang! we spent five days exploring central vietnam, discovering the perfect balance between the modern coastal life in da nang and the nostalgic, lantern-lit streets of hoi an ancient town. we travelled through the region in june, and this travel guide covers everything from relaxing beach vibes and local night markets to getting custom clothes made at a local tailor. if you are currently planning your own vietnam itinerary, this vlog shows you exactly why you cannot skip the central coast. 

in this vlog:

comments.text: Been going to Vietnam since 2001 and Hoi An is best avoided these days. First time in Hoi An there was no coast road from Da Nang, no bridges over the other side of the river and no "traditional" lantern festival. We went back to Hoi An earlier this year after a twelve year absence and I found it rather unpleasant. Liked your vid though.

comments.text: Love the way you capture everything! I'm a new subscriber,  I enjoy how authentic your video looks.  I had some questions, so you did 1 night Da Nang, and 3 nights in Hoi An? Is there a reason you skipped Ba Na Hills/golden bridge? Also, were you happy with the tailored clothes? And would you recommend staying in both Da Nang and Hoi An, or keeping one as the base? Thank you!!

comments.author: @leonandkathy
comments.text: Thank you! We would recommend staying 1-2 nights in Danang if you're keen on a beach holiday, the city is perfect for that! We actually skipped Banana Hills for that very reason, as we wanted to spend more time at the beach. And we're extremely happy with the tailored clothes! You can also check out the tailors' reviews on Google Maps beforehand to see photos of their previous work. That really helped us a lot in making our final decision to choose one :)
